stages.name: Unreached
stages.desc: Coasts no Mediterranean sailor is known to have seen

stages.name: Egypt under Necho
stages.desc: The kingdom of Pharaoh Necho II, ruled from Sais

stages.name: Phoenician-held coasts
stages.desc: Phoenician cities, colonies and trading posts

stages.name: Claimed route, year 1
stages.desc: Red Sea and East African coasts, if the voyage happened

stages.name: Claimed route, year 2
stages.desc: Southern Africa and the Atlantic coast up to the Gulf of Guinea

stages.name: Claimed route, year 3
stages.desc: West Africa and the run north to the Pillars of Heracles

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre and Sidon, the mother cities of the Phoenicians, lead Mediterranean trade
After Megiddo, the Levant briefly falls under Egyptian control
After Carchemish, the Phoenician cities must reckon with Babylon

states.name: Somalia
timeline: The Horn of Africa, beyond Egyptian knowledge
Past the Bab el-Mandeb, the crews round the Horn at Cape Guardafui

states.name: Kenya
timeline: East African coast, unknown to Mediterranean sailors
The north-east monsoon carries the ships south along the coast

states.name: Tanzania
timeline: East African coast and offshore islands
The fleet keeps south, the sun now high overhead at noon

states.name: Morocco
timeline: Phoenician posts at Lixus and on the island of Mogador, on the Atlantic coast
If the crews came north this way, Mogador was the first Phoenician harbour

states.name: Namibia
timeline: Desert coast of the South Atlantic
The cold Benguela current carries the ships north along the desert coast

states.name: South Africa
timeline: The southern tip of Africa
Turning west round the Cape, the crews see the noon sun on their right, in the north

states.name: Libya
timeline: Phoenician trading posts at Lepcis, Oea and Sabratha; Greek Cyrene rises in the east

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage and Utica, Phoenician colonies, command the narrows of the Mediterranean

states.name: Liberia
timeline: Coast of the Gulf of Guinea, ending at Cape Palmas
At Cape Palmas the coast, and the voyage, turn north

states.name: Sudan
timeline: Red Sea shore beyond Egypt's frontier; the Nile valley belongs to Kush
The fleet sails south down the Red Sea

states.name: Eritrea
timeline: Red Sea coast, perhaps part of the land Egyptians had long called Punt
The crews pass the old Egyptian trade route to Punt

states.name: Côte d'Ivoire
timeline: Lagoon coast of the Gulf of Guinea
The fleet follows the lagoon coast west

states.name: Senegal
timeline: Cape Verde, the westernmost point of Africa
Past Cape Verde, against the Canary current and the trade winds

states.name: Nigeria
timeline: The Niger delta and its mangrove creeks
The third year: the fleet heads west along the Gulf of Guinea

states.name: Angola
timeline: Atlantic coast south of the Congo
The fleet passes the mouth of the Congo, Africa's second great river

states.name: Mozambique
timeline: Coast of the Mozambique Channel
The first autumn: the crews may have landed here to sow and wait for harvest

states.name: Cameroon
timeline: Coast below Mount Cameroon
A second autumn halt is possible in the Gulf of Guinea

states.name: Gabon
timeline: Equatorial forest coast
Crossing the equator northward, the sun swings back to the south

states.name: Ghana
timeline: Coast of the Gulf of Guinea
Sailing west in the northern hemisphere, the noon sun is on their left again

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Necho II succeeds his father Psamtik I as pharaoh of the 26th, Saite dynasty
Necho marches into Syria to support the last Assyrian king against Babylon
Defeated at Carchemish, Egypt loses its Asian conquests to Babylon
Necho beats back Nebuchadnezzar's attack on Egypt's eastern border
In the third year the Phoenician crews come back to Egypt, Herodotus says
Necho dies and his son Psamtik II becomes pharaoh

events.title: Necho crowned
events.text: Psamtik I dies and his son Necho II becomes pharaoh at Sais, in the Nile delta.

events.title: Greeks at Naukratis
events.text: Greek traders settle at Naukratis under the Saite kings; their descendants will tell Herodotus Egypt's stories.

events.title: Carthage
events.text: Carthage, a Tyrian colony, is the strongest Phoenician city in the western Mediterranean.

events.title: Tyre
events.text: Tyre, on its island, sends ships to every coast of the Mediterranean and out into the Atlantic.

events.title: A canal begun
events.text: Necho starts a canal from the Nile to the Red Sea; Herodotus says 120,000 workers died before he stopped.

events.title: Fleets on two seas
events.text: Necho builds triremes on the Mediterranean and on the Red Sea, says Herodotus.

events.title: Megiddo
events.text: Josiah, king of Judah, tries to block Necho's march north and is killed at Megiddo.

events.title: Harran
events.text: Necho joins the Assyrians in a failed attempt to retake Harran from the Babylonians.

events.title: Kadytis taken
events.text: Necho takes the city Herodotus calls Kadytis, probably Gaza.

events.title: Judah's new king
events.text: At Riblah, Necho deposes Jehoahaz of Judah and installs Jehoiakim as his vassal.

events.title: Gift to Apollo
events.text: Necho sends the robe he wore on campaign to Apollo's sanctuary at Didyma.

events.title: Carchemish
events.text: The Babylonian crown prince Nebuchadnezzar crushes Necho's army on the Euphrates.

events.title: Rout at Hamath
events.text: The Babylonians catch the fleeing Egyptians at Hamath; Egypt's hold on Syria ends.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar king
events.text: Nebuchadnezzar II succeeds his father as king of Babylon.

events.title: Ashkelon sacked
events.text: Nebuchadnezzar destroys Ashkelon on the coast of Philistia.

events.title: Battle at the border
events.text: Nebuchadnezzar attacks Egypt; the Babylonian Chronicle admits heavy losses on both sides.

events.title: Lepcis
events.text: Phoenician traders work from Lepcis and other harbours on the Libyan coast.

events.title: The fleet sails
events.text: Around this time, Herodotus says, Phoenician crews in Necho's service sail south down the Red Sea.

events.title: Toward Punt
events.text: The crews pass the coasts where Egyptians had sailed for incense since the pyramid age.

events.title: Bab el-Mandeb
events.text: The fleet leaves the Red Sea through the strait into the open ocean.

events.title: Cape Guardafui
events.text: At the Horn of Africa, the coast turns south.

events.title: The monsoon coast
events.text: The north-east winter monsoon blows the ships south along East Africa.

events.title: Across the equator
events.text: South of the equator the noon sun begins to stand in the north.

events.title: First harvest halt
events.text: Each autumn, Herodotus says, the crews landed, sowed grain and waited for the harvest.

events.title: Agulhas current
events.text: A fast southward current speeds the ships along the south-east coast.

events.title: Sun on the right
events.text: Sailing west round the Cape, the crews see the noon sun on their right, in the north.

events.title: Benguela current
events.text: A cold current runs north along the Namib desert coast, helping the ships home.

events.title: Mouth of the Congo
events.text: The fleet passes the mouth of a vast river that stains the sea brown.

events.title: North of the equator
events.text: Crossing the equator northward, the noon sun swings back to the south.

events.title: Mount Cameroon
events.text: A volcano rises over the Gulf of Guinea, the coast's highest peak.

events.title: Niger delta
events.text: The third year: the crews follow the mangrove coast west.

events.title: Sun on the left
events.text: Sailing west north of the equator, the noon sun is on their left once more.

events.title: Lagoon coast
events.text: Long lagoons and surf beaches line the shore.

events.title: Cape Palmas
events.text: At Cape Palmas the coast turns north toward home.

events.title: Cape Verde
events.text: The fleet rounds Africa's westernmost point.

events.title: Against the wind
events.text: North of Cape Bojador, the trade winds and the Canary current run against the ships.

events.title: Mogador
events.text: A Phoenician trading post on an offshore island: the first friendly harbour on the route.

events.title: Lixus
events.text: An old Phoenician town on the Atlantic coast of Morocco.

events.title: Pillars of Heracles
events.text: In the third year the crews pass through the strait into the Mediterranean.

events.title: Home to Egypt
events.text: The Phoenicians report to Necho that they have sailed round Libya.

events.title: Jerusalem surrenders
events.text: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem and carries King Jehoiachin into exile.

events.title: Necho dies
events.text: Necho II dies after fifteen years on the throne; Psamtik II succeeds him.

chartNote: Share of the area of the mapped countries, by their place in the story. Regions are today's countries, used as a grid: no such borders existed. Herodotus is the only source for the voyage and gives no date or route; it is placed around 600 BC as is conventional, and the split of the coast into three years is an illustrative reconstruction of the claim, not evidence of it. Whole countries are coloured though only their coasts are concerned.
chartTitle: Africa's coasts in the story, by area
